atoms.text: Katherine Johnson was a successful mathematician who assisted NASA in their space flights. Thanks to Johnson’s maths, spacecrafts were able to orbit Earth and land on the moon. Her journey to becoming a successful mathematician was an impressive one, despite occasional hardships on the way there.

Johnson was born in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia in 1918. From an early age, she already impressed her teachers with her intellect. Since her town didn’t offer classes for Black Americans after the 8th grade (equivalent to year 9 in the UK), her family moved to a town where she was able to pursue an academic career after receiving her high school diploma at just 14. At age 18, she graduated with degrees in both maths and French at West Virginia State College.

Since her town didn’t offer classes for Black Americans after the 8th grade, equivalent to year 9 in the UK, her family moved to a town where she was able to pursue an academic career, after receiving her high school diploma at just 14. At age 18, she graduated with degrees in both maths and French at West Virginia State College.

atoms.text: In 1952, the young, ambitious mathematician decided to apply for a new job after teaching maths and French for over a decade. Johnson discovered that the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) had begun hiring Black American women to perform and check calculations for certain technological developments. She applied for a position at the Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia and was accepted. Shortly after beginning the job, Johnson mesmerised her superiors with her exceeding curiosity and engaging approach to problem-solving, which is why she was transferred from the Black American section to Langley’s flight research division.

After NACA was renamed into what many know today as NASA, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Johnson was in charge of working on successful space travel for humans. She played an essential role in calculating Alan Shepard’s journey to space in 1961 — the first human space travel voyage in US history. After this success, she went on to work on helping successfully send someone into orbit around Earth in 1962. She even partook in the 1969 Apollo 11 mission to the moon. All in all, Katherine Johnson left an impressionable mark on the history of space travel.
